data.narrative:
SF Compute is a Series A stage semiconductor company founded by Evan Conrad and Alex Gajewski that has raised $52M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 identifiable private peers such as SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor, though the narrow peer set at Series A stage is limited.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $52M total raised as a base value proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage transitions, yielding an implied valuation of $104M. The Peer-Median method was not applicable; while 12 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three qualify within the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier positioning. Public-Comp Anchoring was not applicable because SF Compute's revenue is not on file; the public semiconductor sector shows a 21.0x median P/S multiple across the three public tickers, but cannot be deployed without a disclosed revenue figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M (low) to $120M (high), with a median estimate of $104M. This range is anchored to a single method and should be regarded with appropriate caution. Key uncertainties include the absence of a tight peer comparability set at Series A, undisclosed revenue metrics, and reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than market-derived multiples.
